description: A source of uncertainty in the manner of the Buchla 266: two sections of fluctuating random voltages, a section of quantized random voltages, a section of stored random voltages, and three flip-flops

params.text: How fast that section's random voltage changes, over a range marked 0.05 to 50
How much the second section's random voltage is smoothed, from 0 to 1
Sets n for the quantized section, from 1 to 6
Lets a value that has already come up come up again in the quantized section

inputs.text: A voltage changing how fast that section's random voltage changes
A voltage setting how much the second section's random voltage is smoothed
A pulse produces a new quantized random voltage
A voltage setting n for the quantized section
A pulse produces a new stored random voltage
A pulse flips the output beside it between high and low

outputs.text: A random voltage that glides from one value to the next, marked SMOOTH
A random voltage that steps straight from one value to the next, marked HARD
A random voltage taking one of two to the power of n equally likely values
A random voltage taking one of n plus one equally likely values
A gate that changes between high and low on every pulse arriving at the input beside it

notes: the n plus one output uses a triangular distribution, as though two dice were thrown, and steps by 1V; the two to the power of n output steps by 1/12V.
nothing needs setting up: both fluctuating sections run on their own clocks as soon as the module is placed.
